title: Preventing mediator release
prompt: A laboratory exposes sensitized mast cells to an allergen and measures histamine in the surrounding medium. Pretreatment with cromolyn reduces mediator release compared with an untreated control culture. Which action best explains the preventive effect demonstrated in this experiment?
options: Blockade of muscarinic receptors on airway smooth muscle
Neutralization of circulating IL-5
Irreversible inhibition of cyclooxygenase in platelets
Inhibition of mast-cell degranulation
Direct stimulation of beta-2 receptors
explanation: Cromolyn stabilizes mast cells and limits release of mediators rather than acting as a direct bronchodilator.

distractorExplanations.Inhibition of mast-cell degranulation: Cromolyn stabilizes mast cells and limits release of mediators rather than acting as a direct bronchodilator.
distractorExplanations.Direct stimulation of beta-2 receptors: That is the action of beta-2 agonists.
distractorExplanations.Irreversible inhibition of cyclooxygenas: That is unrelated to cromolyn’s mast-cell effect.

title: An attack already underway
prompt: A patient prescribed inhaled cromolyn for preventive treatment arrives with acute wheezing and difficulty speaking. He says he has repeatedly used cromolyn because it is an asthma medicine. Why has this strategy not provided rapid relief?
options: Cromolyn causes permanent beta-2 receptor blockade
Every asthma medicine has an identical onset of effect
Cromolyn does not reverse established bronchospasm as a rescue bronchodilator
Cromolyn works only when swallowed during an attack
Cromolyn must be mixed with another solution before every use
answer: Cromolyn does not reverse established bronchospasm as a rescue bronchodilator
explanation: An acute attack needs appropriate reliever treatment and assessment; preventive medication does not replace rescue care.

distractorExplanations.Cromolyn does not reverse established br: An acute attack needs appropriate reliever treatment and assessment; preventive medication does not replace rescue care.
distractorExplanations.Cromolyn works only when swallowed durin: Changing to an oral route does not turn it into a rescue bronchodilator.
distractorExplanations.Cromolyn must be mixed with another solu: Unverified mixing is not the explanation and may not be safe.
distractorExplanations.Cromolyn causes permanent beta-2 recepto: It does not block beta-2 receptors.
distractorExplanations.Every asthma medicine has an identical o: Controller and reliever drugs differ in mechanism and onset.

title: An allergic ocular presentation
prompt: A 19-year-old student develops bilateral itchy, watery eyes each spring when pollen counts rise. There is no eye pain, visual change or purulent discharge. A clinician recommends ketotifen eye drops. Which symptom is this formulation intended to relieve?
options: Loss of visual acuity from retinal detachment
Allergy-associated ocular itching
Pain from acute angle-closure glaucoma
Corneal injury from a retained foreign body
Purulent bacterial keratitis
explanation: Ophthalmic ketotifen is used for allergic eye itching; the described symptoms support that indication.

distractorExplanations.Allergy-associated ocular itching: Ophthalmic ketotifen is used for allergic eye itching; the described symptoms support that indication.
distractorExplanations.Pain from acute angle-closure glaucoma: Painful visual symptoms need urgent assessment rather than an allergy-drop substitution.
distractorExplanations.Corneal injury from a retained foreign b: Ketotifen does not remove a foreign body or treat corneal injury.
distractorExplanations.Purulent bacterial keratitis: This requires different assessment and treatment.
distractorExplanations.Loss of visual acuity from retinal detac: Allergy drops do not treat a retinal emergency.

title: Contact lenses and allergy drops
prompt: A 26-year-old soft-contact-lens wearer plans to use ketotifen drops for seasonal eye itching. Her eyes are not red, and she has no pain or visual symptoms. Which administration advice best follows the product guidance?
options: Remove the lenses before dosing and wait at least 10 minutes before reinsertion
Instill the drops directly onto the lenses while they are worn
Use the drops as a contact-lens disinfectant
Use extra drops to treat contact-lens irritation
Keep wearing lenses if the eyes become red
answer: Remove the lenses before dosing and wait at least 10 minutes before reinsertion
explanation: Soft lenses can absorb the preservative; the label specifies removing them and waiting before reinsertion.

distractorExplanations.Remove the lenses before dosing and wait: Soft lenses can absorb the preservative; the label specifies removing them and waiting before reinsertion.
distractorExplanations.Instill the drops directly onto the lens: The product should not be instilled with soft lenses in place.
distractorExplanations.Use the drops as a contact-lens disinfec: Ophthalmic medication is not a disinfecting solution.
distractorExplanations.Use extra drops to treat contact-lens ir: The label excludes contact-lens-related irritation as an indication.
distractorExplanations.Keep wearing lenses if the eyes become r: Red eyes are a reason not to wear contact lenses and to reassess the problem.

title: New symptoms during treatment
prompt: A patient treating presumed seasonal eye allergy with ketotifen develops unilateral eye pain and reduced vision the next morning. Itching had been the initial symptom, but the new symptoms are different. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Increase dosing frequency until vision improves
Assume reduced vision confirms the intended drug effect
Cover the symptoms with contact lenses
Continue unchanged for several weeks before seeking care
Stop self-treatment and obtain prompt eye assessment
answer: Stop self-treatment and obtain prompt eye assessment
explanation: Pain and visual change are warning symptoms; they should not be assumed to be uncomplicated allergy.

distractorExplanations.Stop self-treatment and obtain prompt ey: Pain and visual change are warning symptoms; they should not be assumed to be uncomplicated allergy.
distractorExplanations.Increase dosing frequency until vision i: Exceeding labeled use delays evaluation of potentially serious disease.
distractorExplanations.Assume reduced vision confirms the inten: Visual loss is not a desired therapeutic effect.
distractorExplanations.Cover the symptoms with contact lenses: Lenses do not address the cause and may worsen some ocular problems.
distractorExplanations.Continue unchanged for several weeks bef: New pain and visual change warrant timely assessment.
